analysis: The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md, adding head lines 595-611. The paragraph describes a Gated DeltaNet four-row recurrence prefill kernel for qwen3_5, qwen3_5_moe and prism_hadamard_qwen35. For windows of 16 or more unmasked positions it probes the `packed` and then `rows` kernel once per instantiation, adopts the first that bit-matches `gated_delta_step` on the GPU, and otherwise keeps the stock kernel. Decode, MTP verification, masked updates and short windows stay on the stock kernel. DARKBLOOM_TTFT_GDN_BLOCKED can force a kernel. The supplied units are base text only (lines 798-1637); the changed region at head 595-611 is visible only in the patch excerpt. No code, config, endpoint or deployment changes are included, so no control is altered. Relevant threats are T-041 (prefix-cache and checkpoint state), T-028 and T-056. The doc's claim that selected kernels match stock bit for bit, so recurrent checkpoint state is unchanged, is relevant to the complete-checkpoint SSD cache. Because the cache keys include no kernel identity, any numerical divergence could mix checkpoints across kernels. Whether the actual implementation in GatedDelta.swift enforces bit-exactness cannot be verified from the supplied evidence, so this is recorded as an unverified contract rather than a finding. The probe is a single fixed-window check, so it may not cover all geometries or dtypes. The env override only changes kernel choice and is not in the deadline or serving-profile allowlist context. The next pass should review the actual Swift kernel code, if included in other PR files, for bit-exactness and probe coverage, and for any effect on the prefix-cache or checkpoint identity.
